title: Marked lift bijections for an (RS) fibre square
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $\mathrm{Art}_k=\mathcal C_{k,k}$ and (RS) have the meanings of [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a groupoid-valued pseudofunctor on $\mathrm{Art}_k$ satisfying (RS). For a morphism $f:B\to A$ in $\mathrm{Art}_k$ and $x\in\mathcal F(A)$, let $L_{\mathcal F}(x,B)$ be the set of isomorphism classes of pairs $(y,\alpha)$ with $y\in\mathcal F(B)$ and $\alpha:f_*y\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, where an isomorphism $u$ from $(y,\alpha)$ to $(y',\alpha')$ obeys $\alpha'\circ f_*u=\alpha$. Let $p:A_1\to A$ and $q:A_2\to A$ be morphisms in $\mathrm{Art}_k$, with at least one of $p,q$ surjective, and put $P=A_1\times_A A_2$. For every $x\in\mathcal F(A)$, restriction gives a canonical bijection
$$L_{\mathcal F}(x,P)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\mathcal F}(x,A_1)\times L_{\mathcal F}(x,A_2).$$
If $(x_1,\alpha_1)$ is a fixed marked lift of $x$ to $A_1$, restriction to $A_2$, followed by the marking through $\alpha_1$, gives a canonical bijection
$$L_{\mathcal F}(x_1,P)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\mathcal F}(x,A_2).$$
Both bijections are natural under isomorphisms of the marked objects, under maps between such fibre-square diagrams, and under morphisms of groupoid-valued pseudofunctors commuting coherently with transport (when both pseudofunctors satisfy (RS)).

source.place: Tag 06JH (remark-lift-bijections), using definition-lifts and the (RS) equivalence.

proof.text: Write $p_1=p$, $p_2=q$, $a_i:P\to A_i$ and $r=p_1a_1=p_2a_2$. By [def-weil-field], every ideal of $k$ is zero or $k$, so $k$ is Noetherian; $k$ is finite type over itself, generated by the empty set. Thus [lem-sfb-artin-local-test-algebra] applies with $R=k$: $P$ is an object of $\mathrm{Art}_k$ with the indicated local residue-preserving projections. If only $p$ is surjective, exchange the two indices when applying that statement and (RS); swapping the two factors and inverting the gluing isomorphism identifies the resulting comparison with the original one. Let $E$ be the (RS) functor of [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Its target has objects $(y_1,y_2,\gamma:p_{1*}y_1\cong p_{2*}y_2)$. Define $c_i(y)=c_{p_i,a_i}(y):p_{i*}a_{i*}y\cong r_*y$ and $\delta_y=c_2(y)^{-1}c_1(y)$. Then $E(y)=(a_{1*}y,a_{2*}y,\delta_y)$; a pair $(u_1,u_2)$ is a morphism $E(y)\to E(z)$ exactly when $\delta_z p_{1*}u_1=p_{2*}u_2\delta_y$. The hypothesis (RS) says precisely that every such pair lifts uniquely to an arrow $y\to z$, and every target object is isomorphic to some $E(y)$.

source.place: Tag 06GH (lemma-fiber-product-CLambda); Tag 06JH (remark-lift-bijections); equivalence form of (RS) as in Tag 06J5 (lemma-RS-2-categorical), already the definition used here.

proof.text: For a marked lift $(y,\alpha:r_*y\cong x)$, define $\alpha_i=\alpha c_i(y)$. Restriction sends its class to $([a_{1*}y,\alpha_1],[a_{2*}y,\alpha_2])$. For a marked isomorphism $u:(y,\alpha)\to(z,\alpha')$, naturality of the compositors in [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category] gives $c_i(z)p_{i*}a_{i*}u=r_*u\,c_i(y)$, hence $\alpha'_i p_{i*}a_{i*}u=\alpha_i$. Thus this map is well-defined on classes. Notice the identity $\alpha_2^{-1}\alpha_1=\delta_y$. All products of arrows in this proof mean composition, with the rightmost arrow applied first.

source.place: Tag 06JH (remark-lift-bijections), expanded using the equivalence form of (RS) already assumed in the statement; Tag 06JE (definition-lifts).

proof.text: For surjectivity, take representatives $(y_i,\alpha_i:p_{i*}y_i\cong x)$ of any pair on the right and put $\gamma=\alpha_2^{-1}\alpha_1$. Essential surjectivity in (RS), as defined in [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category], supplies $y\in\mathcal F(P)$ and isomorphisms $v_i:a_{i*}y\cong y_i$ with $\gamma p_{1*}v_1=p_{2*}v_2\delta_y$. Set $\alpha=\alpha_1 p_{1*}v_1 c_1(y)^{-1}$. The displayed compatibility gives also $\alpha=\alpha_2 p_{2*}v_2 c_2(y)^{-1}$. Consequently $v_i$ are marked isomorphisms from the restrictions of $(y,\alpha)$ to $(y_i,\alpha_i)$, proving surjectivity without a choice of a canonical representative.

source.place: Tag 06JH (remark-lift-bijections), expanded using the equivalence form of (RS) already assumed in the statement; Tag 06JE (definition-lifts).

proof.text: For injectivity, suppose $(y,\alpha)$ and $(z,\beta)$ have the same image. Choose marked isomorphisms $u_i:a_{i*}y\cong a_{i*}z$, so $\beta_i p_{i*}u_i=\alpha_i$, where $\alpha_i=\alpha c_i(y)$ and $\beta_i=\beta c_i(z)$. Then $\beta_2\delta_z p_{1*}u_1=\beta_1p_{1*}u_1=\alpha_1=\alpha_2\delta_y=\beta_2p_{2*}u_2\delta_y$. Cancelling the invertible $\beta_2$ gives the compatibility required in step 1. Full faithfulness in (RS) [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category] produces $u:y\to z$ with $a_{i*}u=u_i$. It is invertible since $\mathcal F(P)$ is a groupoid. Naturality of $c_1$ and the equation for $u_1$ give $\beta r_*u=\alpha$. Thus it is a marked isomorphism. This proves injectivity, and hence the first bijection and independence of the inverse from every choice in step 3.

source.place: Tag 06JH (remark-lift-bijections), expanded using the equivalence form of (RS) already assumed in the statement; Tag 06JE (definition-lifts).

proof.text: Fix $(x_1,\alpha_1:p_{1*}x_1\cong x)$. For a lift $(y,\eta:a_{1*}y\cong x_1)$ define its marking on $a_{2*}y$ by $\zeta=\alpha_1p_{1*}\eta\,\delta_y^{-1}:p_{2*}a_{2*}y\cong x$. Naturality of $\delta$ shows this respects marked isomorphisms. Given $(y_2,\alpha_2)$, apply essential surjectivity of (RS) [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category] to $(x_1,y_2,\alpha_2^{-1}\alpha_1)$, obtaining $(y,v_1,v_2)$. Take $\eta=v_1$. The gluing equation gives $\alpha_2p_{2*}v_2=\alpha_1p_{1*}\eta\,\delta_y^{-1}$, proving surjectivity. For injectivity, let $v:a_{2*}y\cong a_{2*}z$ be a marked isomorphism between the images of $(y,\eta)$ and $(z,\theta)$, and put $u_1=\theta^{-1}\eta$. The marking equation for $v$, after cancellation of $\alpha_1$ and rearrangement, is $\delta_zp_{1*}u_1=p_{2*}v\delta_y$. Full faithfulness gives $u:y\cong z$ restricting to $(u_1,v)$, and $\theta a_{1*}u=\eta$ proves that it is marked. This proves the second bijection, including independence from choices.

source.place: Tag 06JH (remark-lift-bijections), expanded using the equivalence form of (RS) already assumed in the statement; Tag 06JE (definition-lifts).

proof.text:
For an isomorphism $h:x\cong x'$, change markings by $\alpha\mapsto h\alpha$. The restriction formula becomes $(h\alpha)c_i=h(\alpha c_i)$, and $(h\alpha_2)^{-1}(h\alpha_1)=\alpha_2^{-1}\alpha_1$. If $h_1:x_1\cong x'_1$ and $\alpha'_1p_{1*}h_1=h\alpha_1$, then $\eta\mapsto h_1\eta$ sends the second-map formula to $h\alpha_1p_{1*}\eta\delta_y^{-1}$. This proves both marked-object naturalities. For a coherent morphism $T:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$, write $t_f:f_*^{\mathcal G}T_B\cong T_Af_*^{\mathcal F}$. Its map on marked lifts is $(y,\alpha)\mapsto(T_By,T_A(\alpha)t_f(y))$. Coherence with the compositors of [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category] reads
$$t_r(y)c_i^{\mathcal G}(T_Py)=T_A(c_i^{\mathcal F}(y))\,t_{p_i}(a_{i*}y)\,p_{i*}^{\mathcal G}(t_{a_i}(y)).$$
Thus $t_{a_i}(y)$ identify the restrictions of $T_Py$ with $T_{A_i}(a_{i*}y)$ as marked objects. Substituting this equality for $i=1,2$ in $\alpha c_i$ and $\alpha_1p_{1*}\eta\delta_y^{-1}$ proves that both restriction maps commute with $T$ on classes. Their inverse maps commute as well, since each restriction map is bijective.

source.place: Tag 06JH (remark-lift-bijections), expanded using the equivalence form of (RS) already assumed in the statement; Tag 06JE (definition-lifts).

proof.text:
Finally take a map of fibre-square diagrams, with morphisms of $\mathrm{Art}_k$ $b_i:A_i\to A'_i$, $b:A\to A'$ satisfying $p'_ib_i=bp_i$, and induced $d:P\to P'$; let $a'_i:P'\to A'_i$ and $r':P'\to A'$. Thus $a'_id=b_ia_i$ and $r'd=br$. Change the base object to $b_*x$, or to an object equipped with a specified isomorphism from $b_*x$. For a marking $\alpha:r_*y\cong x$, the induced marking on $d_*y$ is
$$r'_*d_*y\xrightarrow{c_{r',d}}(r'd)_*y=(br)_*y\xrightarrow{c_{b,r}^{-1}}b_*r_*y\xrightarrow{b_*\alpha}b_*x.$$
For each $i$ the comparison between $a'_{i*}d_*y$ and $b_{i*}a_{i*}y$ is $c_{b_i,a_i}^{-1}c_{a'_i,d}$. Applying $b_i$ to $(a_{i*}y,\alpha c_i(y))$ gives the marking $b_*(\alpha c_{p_i,a_i})c_{b,p_i}^{-1}c_{p'_i,b_i}$. Omitting $b_*\alpha$, we need $c_{b,r}^{-1}c_{r',d}c_{p'_i,a'_i}=b_*(c_{p_i,a_i})c_{b,p_i}^{-1}c_{p'_i,b_i}\,p'_{i*}(c_{b_i,a_i}^{-1}c_{a'_i,d})$ on $p'_{i*}a'_{i*}d_*y$. The associativity axiom of [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category] for $(b,p_i,a_i)$ gives $b_*(c_{p_i,a_i})c_{b,p_i}^{-1}=c_{b,r}^{-1}c_{bp_i,a_i}$; for $(p'_i,b_i,a_i)$, since $p'_ib_i=bp_i$, it gives $c_{bp_i,a_i}c_{p'_i,b_i}=c_{p'_i,b_ia_i}p'_{i*}c_{b_i,a_i}$; for $(p'_i,a'_i,d)$ it gives $c_{r',d}c_{p'_i,a'_i}=c_{p'_i,a'_id}p'_{i*}c_{a'_i,d}$; with $b_ia_i=a'_id$ both sides agree. This proves naturality of the first restriction map. For the second, use the same comparison with $i=1$ on $\eta$ and with $i=2$ on the image; the equality just proved for both indices, substituted in $\alpha_1p_{1*}\eta\delta_y^{-1}$, proves naturality of that restriction map. Postcomposing by the specified base-object isomorphism is step 6. Bijection then implies naturality of both inverses. At least one of $p_1,p_2$ and at least one of $p'_1,p'_2$ is assumed surjective; no surjectivity of $b,b_i$ is used.
